record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.original_question: The MSSM gauge couplings appear to meet near 2 × 10^16 GeV when evolved with the minimal supersymmetric particle content, suggesting a single unified gauge coupling and possibly a simple GUT group such as SU(5), SO(10), SU(6), or E6. Does the MSSM truly unify into a supersymmetric grand unified theory, and can such a theory simultaneously explain charge quantization, matter representations, baryon-number violation, and the observed low-energy couplings?

evidence.quote: Question #13 Does the MSSM unify into a supersymmetric GUT?
By combining GUT’s with supersymmetry in the context of SUSY GUT’s, we then hope to realize the attractive features of GUT’s simultaneously with those of supersymmetry in a single theory.
Performing this extrapolation within the context of the supersymmetric MSSM... one obtains an apparent gauge coupling unification... at the scale MGUT ≈ 2 × 10^16 GeV.
The apparent gauge coupling unification of the MSSM is strong circumstantial evidence in favor of the emergence of a SUSY GUT near 10^16 GeV.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM): a quantum field theory extending the Standard Model gauge group G_SM = SU(3)_C × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y by adding, for every Standard Model fermion, a scalar superpartner of the same gauge quantum numbers, and, for every gauge boson, a fermionic gaugino superpartner, together with two Higgs doublet chiral superfields H_u and H_d and their higgsino partners, with soft supersymmetry breaking terms at the TeV scale. Let g_1(μ), g_2(μ), g_3(μ) denote the running U(1)_Y (in GUT normalization), SU(2)_L, and SU(3)_C gauge couplings, evolved via the two-loop renormalization group equations of the MSSM from the electroweak scale upward.

(a) Determine whether there exists a scale M_GUT (near 2 × 10^16 GeV) at which g_1(M_GUT) = g_2(M_GUT) = g_3(M_GUT) once experimental uncertainties and threshold corrections from supersymmetric and heavy particle spectra are taken into account, and characterize precisely the spectrum constraints required for exact unification.

(b) Decide whether the MSSM is the low-energy limit of a four-dimensional supersymmetric grand unified theory based on a simple gauge group G ⊇ G_SM (such as SU(5), SO(10), SU(6), or E_6) in which:
  (i) one full generation of MSSM matter fits into a (small set of) irreducible representations of G, explaining the observed hypercharge assignments and charge quantization;
  (ii) the proton decay rate induced by baryon-number-violating dimension-5 and dimension-6 operators is consistent with current experimental lower bounds on the proton lifetime;
  (iii) the unified gauge coupling, the running yielding the measured low-energy values of (g_1, g_2, g_3) at the Z-boson mass, and the doublet–triplet splitting problem are all simultaneously and naturally accommodated.

Provide either an explicit construction satisfying (i)–(iii) or a no-go result excluding such a theory.
artifact.status_search_result: No supersymmetric grand unified theory has been experimentally confirmed. Proton decay searches (Super-Kamiokande, Hyper-Kamiokande) continue to constrain and exclude minimal SUSY SU(5) variants, while LHC searches have not observed superpartners at the TeV scale, tightening but not refuting MSSM-based unification scenarios. Gauge coupling unification in the MSSM remains a strong hint, with various SUSY GUT models (flipped SU(5), SO(10), E_6, orbifold GUTs) still viable. The question of whether the MSSM truly arises from a SUSY GUT explaining all the listed features is still open.

status_evidence.title: Proton decay constraints on SUSY GUTs
status_evidence.snippet: Super-Kamiokande limits on p → K+ ν̄ severely constrain minimal SUSY SU(5); extended models remain viable.
status_evidence.claim: Minimal SUSY GUTs are constrained but not ruled out; the unification question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Status of supersymmetry after the LHC Run 2
status_evidence.snippet: No supersymmetric particles have been discovered; gauge coupling unification in MSSM still phenomenologically attractive.
status_evidence.claim: MSSM SUSY GUT scenarios are not experimentally confirmed nor excluded.
